paragraphs.text: Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive inborn error of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation (den Boer et al., 2002). LCHAD activity resides in the alpha subunit of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (Sims et al., 1995). Affected children present in infancy or early childhood with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, hepatopathy, cardiomyopathy, hypotonia, and sudden death; pigmentary retinopathy and peripheral neuropathy also occur (Tyni et al., 1997; den Boer et al., 2002). Mothers carrying affected fetuses may develop acute fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome (Ibdah et al., 1999).

checks.evidence_quote: LCHAD deficiency is a rare, autosomal recessive inborn error of fatty acid oxidation.
checks.explanation: Abstract states autosomal recessive inborn error of fatty acid oxidation but does not specify 'mitochondrial'.

checks.claim: LCHAD activity resides in the alpha subunit of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein.
checks.evidence_quote: this activity is present on the C-terminal portion of the alpha subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein

checks.claim: Children with LCHAD deficiency present in infancy or early childhood with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, hepatopathy, cardiomyopathy, hypotonia, and sudden death.
checks.evidence_quote: Thirty-nine patients (78%) presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, the classical features of a fatty acid oxidation disorder. Eleven patients (22%) presented with chronic problems, consisting of failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, cholestatic liver disease, and/or hypotonia.
checks.explanation: Hypoketotic hypoglycemia, liver disease, hypotonia, presentation in infancy (up to 26 months) and high mortality are given; cardiomyopathy and sudden death are not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.evidence_quote: While carrying fetuses with the Glu474Gln mutation, 79 percent of the heterozygous mothers had fatty liver of pregnancy or the HELLP syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Tyni et al. (1997) reported 13 patients with LCHAD deficiency, all homozygous for the common G1528C mutation. At presentation the patients had had hypoglycemia, cardiomyopathy, muscle hypotonia, and hepatomegaly during the first 2 years of life. Seven patients had recurrent metabolic crises and 6 had a steadily progressive course. Two patients had cholestatic liver disease, 1 had peripheral neuropathy, and 6 had retinopathy with focal pigmentary aggregations or retinal hypopigmentation. Most patients had lactic acidosis, increased serum creatine kinase activity, and low serum carnitine. Neuroradiologic studies showed bilateral periventricular or focal cortical lesions in 3 patients and brain atrophy in 1. Only 1 patient, who had had dietary treatment for 9 years, was alive at age 14 years; all others died before 2 years of age.

Of 19 children with isolated LCHAD deficiency, who presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver, 8 were homozygous for the glu474-to-gln (E474Q) mutation and 11 were compound heterozygous for this mutation and a different mutation on the other allele. While carrying fetuses with the E474Q mutation, 79% of the heterozygous mothers had fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome.

agent.process_note: I opened all 30 papers. Only Elizondo et al. (2020) was available as full text, and I read it all, including the genotype table. Twenty-five papers were abstracts only, and 4 (Wanders 1989, Uusimaa 1997, Thiel 1999, Carpenter and Wilcken 1999) had only a title, so I cited those by their titles alone. I searched for 'HADHA' to establish the gene name, which only Baskin (2010) and Elizondo (2020) use; the earlier papers call it the alpha subunit of the trifunctional protein. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the intro gives no gene MIM number. The chromosome location (2p, or 2p24.1-23.3) comes from IJlst et al. (1996). The amino acid numbering of the common mutation differs between papers: E510Q is the precursor numbering (IJlst 1994, Elizondo), E474Q the mature-protein numbering (Sims, Ibdah), and Baskin gives the cDNA position as c.1526G>C. I report each paper's notation as written. For the C1132T nonsense mutation (Sims 1995), the abstract does not name the original amino acid, so the variant is named only at the nucleotide level. The abstracts do not report ancestry or consanguinity except for the 'black boy' in Fryburg (1994). Hagenfeldt (1990) describes only a 'suspected' beta-oxidation defect, and I reported it that way.
